Imagine a car. The faster it goes, the much longer it takes to stop. A simple straight line might not perfectly show this "curvy" relationship. Our goal is to build models that can bend and capture these real-world patterns, making them smarter than just a simple straight line.

To bend our simple lines, we add "curvy" features like x squared. This helps models fit complex data. But too many curves make the line wiggle wildly, fitting noise too closely. We use a 'leash' called regularisation, like Ridge or Lasso, to tame these wiggles and keep our models simpler.

For example, trying to fit a simple straight line to curvy car data will underfit, performing poorly. A perfectly bent line, like a parabola, works well. But a super wiggly line tries to hit every single noisy dot, leading to huge errors on new, unseen data, which is extreme overfitting.

Remember this key tip for your exams: in models like Ridge, a larger alpha means stronger regularisation. But for Logistic Regression, a smaller C means stronger regularisation! Don't mix them up. So, we learned to bend lines and tame wiggles for better predictions!
